segments.tts: One move had a one-in-ten-thousand chance. An AI played it anyway.

March 2016, Seoul. Google DeepMind's AlphaGo takes on Lee Sedol – winner of eighteen world titles – at Go, a game with more possible positions than atoms in the universe. Over two hundred million people watch.
Game two, move thirty-seven. AlphaGo plays a stone that commentators first think is a mistake. It wins the game – and overturns centuries of Go wisdom.
But in game four, Lee strikes back with his own one-in-ten-thousand move – "God's Touch" – and wins.
AlphaGo took the match four to one. But both sides showed us something new.
